messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: prod-gpu-eu queue=5.3k, p99 latency=2.7s, autoscaler attempts=46, failures=38. Paging @Lara :rotating_light:
Lara (oncall): ack. looking at router traces. are customers timing out or getting 5xx? :eyes:
Pri (sre): router shows TTL throttles and 502/503 spike starting 21:12 UTC. ~12 tenants affected, some timeouts on long-poll streams. support alerted.
Dev (eng-runtime): cluster events show repeated FailedScheduling: "0/140 nodes are available: 60 Insufficient gpu-mig, 40 node(s) had incompatible MIG profiles". Autoscaler spun up nodes but many have 1g slices while critical pods request 7g or 4g. Looks like template drift across AZs -> MIG fragmentation + stranded slices.
Lara (oncall): ugh. that explains queued requests. what's stranded %?
Dev (eng-runtime): telemetry: GPU util=69%, stranded_mig_capacity ~21% (MIG instances present but unusable due to size mismatch). Autoscaler log: 46 scale-up attempts, 38 rejected with reason "mig_profile_mismatch".
Pri (sre): support: top impacted tenants: metricops (18% error rate), formflow (13%), shopkit (11%). Drafting status update: "Investigating elevated errors on generation endpoints during autoscaler activity." ETA 2h.
Lara (oncall): immediate runbook -> quick triage (order matters):
 - 21:18: cordon + drain one mixed node (gpunode-502) to stop scheduling there
 - 21:20: evict best-effort/cron pods in prod-batch to free larger MIG slices
 - 21:25: bump autoscaler max from 160 -> 220 to allow more correct-profile nodes to come up
 - 21:30: patch node-template for prod-gpu to standardize mig-profile=7g.8gb (fast reprovision)
 - 21:45: if still pending, enable scheduler flag allowMixedMigPacking=true for low-priority pods only (last resort)
Dev (eng-runtime): running cordon/drain: `kubectl cordon gpunode-502 && kubectl drain gpunode-502 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`
Dev (eng-runtime): node label dump & nvidia-smi snippet:
```
kubectl get nodes -l pool=prod-gpu -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,PROFILE:.metadata.labels.mig-profile

gpunode-498   7g.8gb
gpunode-502   mix(1g,7g)
gpunode-510   1g.10gb
```
```
# nvidia-smi mig -l output (sample)
GPU 0: A100-40GB
 Instance 1: 7g.8gb - used 0MB
 Instance 2: 1g.10gb - used 2,100MB
```
Dev (eng-runtime): autoscaler template drift confirmed: some AZ templates were changed to 1g to save costs. Kicking off node-template rollback + provisioning 18 nodes with 7g.8gb. Also preparing admission webhook to prefer schedule critical pods onto nodes with matching slices.
Pri (sre): posting status: "Mitigations running: draining mixed nodes, provisioning homogeneous nodes, evicting non-critical jobs. Monitoring queue and router." Updates at 21:35 / 22:00 UTC.
incident-bot: Autoscaler: 46 requests, 38 failed due to template_mismatch_mig_profile. Estimated stranded capacity 20-25%.
Lara (oncall): Dev, can you force-schedule critical pods to existing 7g nodes while new ones come up? Perhaps patch pod tolerations/affinity temporarily?
Dev (eng-runtime): yes — applying a short-lived mutating patch to label priority-critical pods with nodeAffinity to mig-profile=7g.8gb, and marking non-critical pods preemptible. Doing that now.
Dev (eng-runtime): patch applied. also bumping autoscaler max now. cloud-init jobs started to create 18 nodes.
Theo (next-oncall): I'm warming up; will take handoff in 40m. Anything I should watch?
Lara (oncall): watch queue length, router 5xx, autoscaler failure rate. If the admission patch causes unexpected scheduling loops, kill it. I'll handoff once queue <1k and errors < baseline.
Dev (eng-runtime): new nodes Registering: 6/18 Ready with mig-profile=7g.8gb. Scheduler started placing pending pods. queue dropped 5.3k -> 1.2k in 11m. 5xx down to near-baseline for most tenants.
Pri (sre): support updated status page, AMs notified for metricops/formflow/shopkit. No major SLA breaches yet; tracking closely.
Lara (oncall): any migration errors?
Dev (eng-runtime): a couple of evicted batch jobs restarted with OOMs, non-customer. No customer-facing failures after placements. We did see 2 pods fail to pull image during reschedule; restarted fine.
incident-bot: Incident severity downgraded to S2 at 21:40 UTC — queue <1.5k, error rates improving.
Lara (oncall): prepping post-incident actions:
 - Create INC-3342 and link logs/traces
 - Enforce standard MIG profile across prod auto-scaling templates (infra)
 - Add pre-scale validation in autoscaler to check pending pod MIG requests vs candidate node template
 - Add alert for stranded_mig_capacity > 10% and for autoscaler_mismatch_rate > 5%
Theo (next-oncall): taking over in 30m. Will own the postmortem and follow up with infra to freeze templates.
status-bot: Status updated: "Impact reduced; monitoring. Next update 22:00 UTC."
Lara (oncall): handing off to @Theo. leaving notes and commands in incident doc. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
Theo (next-oncall): taking it. will monitor for 2 hours and follow up with infra.
Pri (sre): logged customer list and times in incident ticket. Will coordinate post-incident comms.
